question.problem:
$\qquad$ $x$ is a multiple of $5$ or $y$ divides $24$.

What is the negation of the composite predicate above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that

$$
\neg ( A \lor B) = \neg A \land \neg B.
$$

So, the negation of "$x$ is a multiple of $5$ or $y$ divides $24$" is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(x\text{ is a multiple of [math]5[/math] or }y\text{ divides }24) & ≡¬(x\text{ is a multiple of }5∨y\text{ divides }24) \\  & ≡¬(x\text{ is a multiple of }5)∧¬(y\text{ divides }24) \\  & ≡x\text{ is not a multiple of }5∧y\text{ does not divide }24 \\  & ≡x\text{ is not a multiple of }5\text{ and }y\text{ does not divide }24.\end{aligned}
$$
